difficulty.description: No formal official grade found. Naturkartan describes the stage as short but strenuous, especially rocky and muddy in rain. Field reports repeatedly mention stones, mud, slippery duckboards, wet rock slabs, dense vegetation, and a steep rocky descent into Njunjes.

routeType.directionForImport: Tarrekaise to Njunjes, matching STF north-to-south section order and Naturkartan BD71 stored direction
routeType.descriptionForApp: A short but rough Tarradalen stage from Tarrekaise to Njunjes. The route leaves the Tarrekaise hut area through dense mountain birch and high vegetation, follows the north side of Tarraure and Luoppal with views toward Hilldo and Tarradalen, then climbs onto a more open plateau before a steep, rocky descent to STF Njunjes above Tarraätno. Wet weather can make the rocky ground, mud, boardwalks and descent noticeably slower than the distance suggests.

rules.rule: The Pärlälvens fjällurskog destination page allows hiking, camping and fires, subject to no damage/disturbance and other applicable laws. County/local fire bans override normal fire permission.

No Pärlälven-specific dog ban was found, but the reserve is reindeer-herding land. Dogs must be kept under strict control; Länsstyrelsen's 2026 notice says dogs in reindeer-herding areas must be leashed/enclosed where reindeer are present and herding is allowed, and general wildlife rules restrict loose dogs 1 March-20 August.

Fishing and hunting are allowed in Pärlälvens fjällurskog only under applicable laws and permits. Tarraure, Luoppal and Tarraätno water-specific rules must be checked before any app fishing context is published.

The Pärlälvens reserve decision allows aircraft landing in the reserve context and Fiskflyg lists Tarrekaise/Njunjes pickup-dropoff service. No Pärlälven-specific drone ban was found in this pass, but Transportstyrelsen/LFV drone rules and nearby national-park restrictions remain dynamic and must be checked before publication.

Do not rely on mobile coverage. STF Tarrekaise says there is no mobile coverage; STF Njunjes says Telia GSM is relatively good, card and Swish may work if coverage works, and a safety room/help phone remains available.

stageSpecificSafety.notes: Naturkartan calls Tarrekaise-Njunjes short but strenuous, with rocky and muddy ground in rain. Field reports support this with rocks, mud, slippery duckboards, wet stones and dense vegetation.
Official and field sources describe a climb to a plateau after Luoppal followed by a steep, rocky descent toward Njunjes. Wet stones on the descent were specifically flagged in a 2018 field report.
STF Njunjes closed early for winter on 2026-04-12 because river ice by the hut was too weak; the two-bed safety room remained. This is a winter/currentness safety note, not a summer closure.

Länsstyrelsen's 2026-04-22 current-mountain information said route checking had stopped because snow and ice deteriorated, with unsafe ice and rapid changes on lakes and watercourses. This is seasonal context and must be rechecked for publication/travel.
stageSpecificSafety.confidence: high for dated notice, dynamic for current impact

stageSpecificSafety.notes: Pärlälvens fjällurskog can be periodically closed due to military activity; Länsstyrelsen says to contact Försvarsmakten. No stage-specific military closure was found on 2026-04-29, but this remains a must-check before publication/travel.
